description.value: The study compared clinical apathy profiles and examined relationships between apathy and FDG-PET brain metabolism in behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia, Alzheimer's disease, and healthy controls.

spans.text: Our main purpose was to compare the clinical apathy profile with the LARS among patients with bvFTD and AD and analyze the relationship between apathy and brain metabolism, using positron emission tomography imaging with 18F fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG-PET).

description.value: A cross-sectional observational study of patients with bvFTD and AD and healthy controls recruited between April 2013 and October 2014.

spans.text: A total of 114 participants were included.

Participants with clinical criteria of AD and bvFTD were recruited from the Cognitive and Behavioral Neurology Unit at Hospital Clínico San Carlos (Madrid, Spain), between April 2013 and October 2014.
Patient diagnoses included 42 individuals with AD and 42 with bvFTD (34 isolated bvFTD; four FTD associated with motoneuron disease; four phenocopies).

The LARS includes 33 items grouped in nine domains or subscales (“Reduction in everyday productivity,” “Lack of interest,” “Lack of initiative,” “Extinction of novelty seeking,” “Motivation,” “Blunting of emotional responses,” “Lack of concern,” “Poor social life,” and “Extinction of self-awareness”) that can be combined to calculate four factors or dimensions of apathy: “intellectual curiosity,” “emotion,” “action initiation,” and “self-awareness” (Sockeel et al., 2006).
